::: {.callout-note}
## What this document is

A **task-specific recipe** for adding a new FS bundle (`fs2`,
`fs3`, ...) to an existing study. Linear walkthrough; each step
has copy-paste commands and verification.

Worked example uses `fs2`, but the same recipe applies to any
new bundle name.

For broader framework concepts, see
[README.qmd](README.qmd). For day-to-day operations on existing
configs, see [simulation_workflow.qmd](simulation_workflow.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Working environment

This recipe assumes **macOS** and writes commands accordingly.
Run all commands from the package root:

```bash
cd ~/Documents/GitHub/forestsearch
```
:::

# Step 1 — Confirm helper scripts are executable

After downloading shell scripts through a browser, macOS strips
the execute bit. Set it on all simulation scripts at once:

```bash
chmod +x quarto/simulations/*.sh
```

Verify:

```bash
ls -l quarto/simulations/*.sh
```

Each line should show `-rwx` permissions on the left. If any line
shows just `-rw-`, repeat the `chmod` command.

::: {.callout-warning}
This is a recurring step — every time you re-download a script,
permissions reset. The fix never changes.
:::

# Step 2 — Define what the new bundle represents

Before touching any files: write a one-sentence answer to
"what does `fs2` do that `fs1` doesn't?"

Examples:

- `fs2` constrains `max_subgroups_search` from 10 to 5 (smaller
  candidate space)
- `fs2` raises `pconsistency.threshold` from 0.80 to 0.90
  (stricter consistency)
- `fs2` changes `stop_threshold` from 0.90 to 0.95 (more
  aggressive early stopping)

You'll write this in the `Regime:` line of the new params file
in Step 3.

# Step 3 — Create the new params file

Copy `fs1_params.R` as a starting point:

```bash
cp quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs1_params.R \
   quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs2_params.R
```

Now open the new file in RStudio and make these four edits:

## 3.1 Rename the function

Search-and-replace `get_fs1_params` → `get_fs2_params`.

There should be exactly one function definition and (potentially)
references in the roxygen `@title`/`@param` blocks above it.
RStudio's "Replace All" handles all occurrences.

## 3.2 Update the regime header comment

The header has a `# Regime:` line. Edit it to capture your
one-sentence definition from Step 2:

```r
# Regime: fs2 — constrained search, focused candidate space.
#
# Designed for: more conservative subgroup identification with
# tighter consistency requirements.
#
# Differs from fs1 in:
#   - max_subgroups_search = 5 (vs fs1's 10)
#   - pconsistency.threshold = 0.90 (vs fs1's 0.80)
```

This block is auto-extracted by `fsparams_summary.qmd` and shown
above the comparison table, so make it useful.

## 3.3 Edit the parameter values

Change only the values that distinguish fs2 from fs1. Leave the
rest unchanged.

## 3.4 Verify the file loads cleanly

In R Console (from the package root):

```r
source("quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs2_params.R")
fs_params <- get_fs2_params(sg_focus = "hr")
str(fs_params)
```

If `source()` and the function call complete without error and
`str()` shows the parameter list, the file is well-formed.

Also test the `sg_focus`-dependent path:

```r
get_fs2_params(sg_focus = "hrMaxSG")$stop_threshold
# Should be NULL
get_fs2_params(sg_focus = "hr")$stop_threshold
# Should be your fs2 stop_threshold value (e.g., 0.95)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Common mistake: forgot to rename the function

If you see:

```
Error in get_fs2_params(sg_focus = "hr") :
  could not find function "get_fs2_params"
```

You forgot Step 3.1 — the function inside `fs2_params.R` is
still named `get_fs1_params`. Rename it and re-source.
:::

# Step 4 — Spawn the per-config qmds

One command propagates the new bundle across all `sg_focus` configs:

```bash
./quarto/simulations/spawn_fs_bundle.sh fs1 fs2
```

Expected output ends with:

```
Done. Spawned 5 new qmd(s).

Next steps:
  1. Spot-check one of the new qmds to verify substitutions.
  2. Render each in 'full' mode (one render per qmd):
       quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_hr_fs2.qmd
       ...
```

The script does several safety checks before spawning:

- Verifies `_fsparams/fs2_params.R` exists
- Warns if `get_fs2_params()` is not yet defined inside it
- Refuses to overwrite any `*_fs2.qmd` files that already exist

If you're prompted with a `Continue anyway? [y/N]` warning, it
means the function rename in Step 3.1 wasn't done — you can
either answer `n`, fix `fs2_params.R`, and re-run, or answer
`y` (the spawn proceeds, but you'll get errors at render time).

## Spot-check one spawned qmd

Open one of the new qmds (any will do) and confirm:

- `BUNDLE_PATH` line points at `..._fs2.rds`
- `source()` line points at `_fsparams/fs2_params.R`
- The function call is `get_fs2_params(...)`
- Validation-check string in the mode-handoff chunk references `_fs2`

The spawn script handles these via token substitution; visual
spot-check is cheap insurance.

# Step 5 — Set each qmd to `full` render mode

Each new qmd defaults to `sim_mode <- "auto"`. For production
renders you need `sim_mode <- "full"`.

Open each of the five new qmds in RStudio and change:

```r
sim_mode <- "auto"
```

to:

```r
sim_mode <- "full"
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Speed up the edits

In RStudio, open all five files (Ctrl+P or Cmd+P, then type
`fs2`). For each: jump to the setup chunk, change the line,
save. About 30 seconds total.
:::

# Step 6 — Run the render queue

This is the slow step (roughly 2 hours per qmd × 5 = 10 hours).
Use `caffeinate` to keep the Mac awake and the render queue to
run them sequentially.

```bash
caffeinate -s ./quarto/simulations/render_queue.sh \
  quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.qmd
```

What this does:

- `caffeinate -s` keeps the system from sleeping while the
  command runs (lid-closure still won't sleep on AC power)
- `render_queue.sh` runs each qmd one at a time, full machine
  resources for each, continues past failures
- Logs go to `quarto/simulations/queue_<timestamp>.log` (top-level)
  and `quarto/simulations/actg175/logs/render_<stem>_<timestamp>.log`
  (per-job)

## Watch progress mid-stream

From a second Terminal window:

```bash
tail -f quarto/simulations/queue_*.log
```

Shows real-time output as the queue runs.

## What the queue produces per qmd

When a render succeeds, you'll see:

```
Bundle saved to: actg175_binary_m1_harm_hr_fs2.rds
  H1: M.M min, N rows, 0 failed
  H0: M.M min, N rows, 0 failed
```

The `0 failed` part matters — if it's nonzero, investigate before
trusting the bundle.

## If you need to disconnect from the terminal

For "launch and forget" mode (e.g., overnight from a remote
session you'll close):

```bash
nohup caffeinate -s ./quarto/simulations/render_queue.sh \
  quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.qmd \
  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
```

Then `tail -f quarto/simulations/queue_*.log` later from any
new terminal.

# Step 7 — Recover from queue failures (if any)

If the queue summary at the end shows failures:

```
Succeeded: 4 / 5
Failed: 1 / 5
  ✗ quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMinSG_fs2.qmd
```

Check the per-job log for that qmd:

```bash
cat quarto/simulations/actg175/logs/render_actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMinSG_fs2_*.log
```

Most common failure modes:

| Symptom in log | Likely cause | Fix |
|----------------|--------------|-----|
| `could not find function "get_fs2_params"` | Step 3.1 missed | Rename function in `fs2_params.R`, re-run failed qmd only |
| `stop_threshold = 0.9 reset to NULL for sg_focus = ...` (1000+ times) | Stale fs1-style override in qmd | Check spawned qmd matches recipe; spawn script should prevent this |
| `object '<some_var>' not found` | A typo introduced in `fs2_params.R` | Fix typo, re-run failed qmd |

To re-run only the failed qmd:

```bash
caffeinate -s quarto render \
  quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMinSG_fs2.qmd
```

(No need for the full queue script — `quarto render` works
directly for a single file.)

# Step 8 — Switch each qmd back to `auto` mode

After all five qmds have rendered successfully:

Open each `*_fs2.qmd` and change `sim_mode <- "full"` back to
`sim_mode <- "auto"`. This prevents accidental re-runs (which
would overwrite the bundles).

# Step 9 — Back up the new bundles

Copy the fresh bundles to your backup directory:

```bash
cd quarto/simulations/actg175
cp actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.rds _backups/
```

Once committed to git, the `.rds` files are also recoverable from
history. The `_backups/` copy is belt-and-suspenders for catastrophic
overwrites.

# Step 10 — Update cross-cut summaries

Two summary documents need to know about `fs2`:

## 10.1 The focus-by-fs cross-cut

Open
`quarto/simulations/actg175/_summaries/actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fsAll_summary.qmd`

In the setup chunk, append `"fs2"` to the `fs_levels` vector:

```r
fs_levels <- c("fs1", "fs2")
```

Re-render:

```bash
quarto render \
  quarto/simulations/actg175/_summaries/actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fsAll_summary.qmd
```

The unified H1 OC table now has rows for both `fs1` and `fs2`,
grouped by `sg_focus × fs`.

## 10.2 The FS parameter summary

This document auto-discovers `fs*_params.R` files — no edits.
Just re-render:

```bash
quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fsparams_summary.qmd
```

The "Differences only" table now has actual content (parameters
that differ between fs1 and fs2).

# Step 11 — Commit and push

```bash
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs2_params.R
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.qmd
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.rds
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.html
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/_summaries/  # if updated
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fsparams_summary.html
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/_backups/

git commit -m "Add fs2 bundle: <one-line description from Step 2>"
git push
```

# Quick reference

The whole recipe condensed:

```bash
# Setup (once per machine after downloading new scripts)
chmod +x quarto/simulations/*.sh

# Define the new bundle
cp quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs1_params.R \
   quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs2_params.R
# Edit fs2_params.R: rename function, update Regime, change values

# Verify in R Console
# source("quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fs2_params.R")
# get_fs2_params(sg_focus = "hr")

# Spawn qmds
./quarto/simulations/spawn_fs_bundle.sh fs1 fs2

# Set each new qmd to sim_mode <- "full" in RStudio

# Run the queue (slow)
caffeinate -s ./quarto/simulations/render_queue.sh \
  quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.qmd

# Set each new qmd back to sim_mode <- "auto"

# Back up bundles
cp quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_*_fs2.rds \
   quarto/simulations/actg175/_backups/

# Update fs_levels in cross-cut summary, re-render summaries
quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/_summaries/actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fsAll_summary.qmd
quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/fsparams_summary.qmd

# Commit and push
git add quarto/simulations/actg175/
git commit -m "Add fs2 bundle: <description>"
git push
```
